headline: KSE-100 extends its winning streak to a fifth straight session, climbing 830 points to close above 172,000 on easing Iran-US tensions and softer oil, even as Wall Street slides and the 10-year Treasury yield rockets to a 19-year high on hawkish Fed signals and crude's snap-back above $103
mood: Cautiously constructive locally · yields and Hormuz the swing factors globally

five_things.html: The KSE-100 rose 830.43 points (+0.48%) on Wednesday to close at 172,232.51 — its fifth consecutive positive session and highest close since early September — after touching an intraday high of 172,762.41. Volume jumped to 773.59 million shares worth Rs26.45 billion (from 641.83 million/Rs18.47 billion), the heaviest turnover since 4 September, as 262 stocks advanced against 196 decliners. Refineries led on Pakistan Refinery's upper circuit, with FFC, UBL, MEBL, ATRL and ENGROH adding roughly 493 index points combined; market capitalisation rose Rs84 billion to Rs19.178 trillion. Topline Securities and Arif Habib's Ali Najib both cited easing international oil prices and improving US-Iran diplomatic signals as the catalyst. Business Recorder and Daily Independent confirm the print.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Slides on Yield Spike
five_things.html: US equities fell across the board Wednesday: the S&P 500 closed at 7,706.03 (−0.76%), the Dow dropped 1.03% to 51,511.59 and the Nasdaq lost 0.69% to 26,936.04, pressured by a surging Treasury yield curve, a weak five-year note auction and hotter-than-expected business-activity data. McDonald's (−4.89%), Alphabet (−4.68%) and Home Depot (−2.80%) led losses while Salesforce (+1.84%), Chevron (+1.38%) and Boeing (+0.95%) held up. Yahoo Finance and Motley Fool confirm the close.

The 10-year Treasury yield jumped over 13bps to 5.10%, its highest level since 2007, while the 2-year climbed past 4.92% on stronger-than-expected US activity surveys, hawkish commentary from Fed Governor Michael Barr on the need for further hikes, and a poorly received five-year note auction — compounding September's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%. CNBC and NBC News confirm the move.

five_things.chip: Oil Snaps Losing Streak on Hormuz Standoff
five_things.html: Brent rose 3.9% to $103.08 and WTI gained 1.8% to $92.16, snapping a five-day losing streak after Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed at the UN that Tehran "will not surrender," dimming hopes of a near-term reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. The IEA has called the ongoing disruption the largest in the history of the global oil market, with over 10 mb/d of Gulf output still shut in and Kuwait's production down roughly a quarter on lost transit capacity. CNBC and AGBI confirm.

five_things.chip: Gold and Silver Slide as Dollar Firms
five_things.html: Gold fell to $4,290 (−1.5% / −$66.70 on the day) and silver tumbled 3.1% to $65.06 as a hawkish Fed narrative firmed the dollar and lifted real yields, denting precious metals despite the region's geopolitical backdrop. Fortune and USAGOLD confirm the pullback.
five_things.sentiment: pulling back on a firmer dollar

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's macro backdrop remains a study in contrasts: the KSE-100 notched a fifth straight gain to 172,232.51 even as August CPI accelerated to 11.15% y/y from 9.2% in July — food (+13.89%) and transport (+20.17%) the main drivers — pulling headline inflation back into double digits and well above the SBP's 5-7% target band. The SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% at its 14 September MPC meeting, while 6-month KIBOR sits at 11.72/11.97% (bid/offer). The IMF mission began talks this week on the fourth EFF review, with roughly $1.2 billion potentially unlocked (a $1 billion EFF tranche plus $200 million under the RSF) contingent on energy-sector reform, circular-debt targets and the Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill now before the Senate. Business Recorder and Daily Independent confirm.
matrix.gcc_html: The Gulf's non-oil economies are outrunning the region's energy disruption: Saudi Arabia's PMI held at 56.6 in September, a 25th straight month of private-sector growth, while the UAE's non-oil PMI hit 55.3 in August, its fastest pace since December 2024, even as the Strait of Hormuz standoff keeps over 10 mb/d of Gulf crude output shut in and Kuwait's production down roughly 25%. Saudi's PIF has approved its 2026-2030 strategy, prioritising private-capital mobilisation and portfolio efficiency as Vision 2030 shifts from rapid build-out to sustained value creation. Gulf News and PIF confirm.
matrix.global_html: The dominant global theme is the bond market: the 10-year Treasury yield's surge to 5.10%, a 19-year high, reflects a hawkish Fed (September's 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00%, with Governor Barr flagging more to come), resilient US activity data and a weak five-year auction — a combination that is repricing risk assets even as equities stay resilient on an AI-led earnings narrative. Separately, Washington's tariff agenda widens: a 100% duty on patented pharmaceuticals and expanded Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods both take effect 29 September. CNBC and Wiley Trade Compliance confirm.

legislative.policy_html: Pakistan Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — tabled in the Senate and now before the Standing Committee on Finance and Revenue, adding fiscal safeguards, governance reforms and disclosure requirements ahead of the IMF's fourth EFF review
legislative.impact_html: Wins: institutional investors and IMF programme compliance, transparency advocates. Loses: SOE management facing tighter oversight, patronage-linked appointments.

legislative.policy_html: PIF's 2026-2030 strategy — approved by the PIF board, shifting from rapid build-out toward private-capital mobilisation and portfolio efficiency as non-oil PMIs hit multi-month highs despite Hormuz-driven output cuts
legislative.sectors: Tourism, construction, financial services, oil & gas
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Saudi/UAE non-oil diversification plays — tourism, construction, banks. Loses: Gulf oil producers absorbing Hormuz-linked output cuts, Kuwait's export-constrained energy sector.

legislative.policy_html: US tariff expansion — a 100% duty on patented pharmaceuticals and ingredients, plus widened Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods, both effective 29 September 2026
legislative.impact_html: Wins: domestic US pharma manufacturers and import-substitution producers. Loses: multinational drugmakers reliant on imported APIs, Canadian exporters, US healthcare payers facing higher costs.

levels.support_note: Wednesday's intraday low; deeper support near 170,900
levels.resistance_note: Wednesday's intraday high; then the 173,500 psychological level

desk_stance_html: The desk stays constructively biased on the KSE-100 heading into Thursday, with refineries, E&P and select banks likely to extend Wednesday's leadership so long as Hormuz headlines don't deteriorate further; a close above 172,760 would open a run at 173,500, while a reversal below 171,850 would flag stalling momentum. Globally, the surge in US yields to 19-year highs is the bigger risk to sentiment — a hawkish Fed and elevated oil keep the path for local rate relief narrow even as the IMF's fourth EFF review gets underway. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

linkedin_text:
KSE-100 extends its winning streak to five sessions — but the real story today is in the bond market.

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street slid Wednesday as the 10-year Treasury yield rocketed to 5.10%, a 19-year high, on hawkish Fed commentary and a weak five-year auction. S&P 500 -0.76% to 7,706.03, Dow -1.03% to 51,511.59, Nasdaq -0.69% to 26,936.04. Oil snapped a five-day losing streak — Brent +3.9% to $103.08, WTI +1.8% to $92.16 — after Iran's president vowed at the UN that Tehran "will not surrender," dimming hopes of a Hormuz reopening. Gold fell to $4,290 (-1.5%) and silver dropped 3.1% to $65.06 as the dollar firmed.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 rose 830 points (+0.48%) to 172,232.51 — a fifth straight gain and the heaviest volume since 4 September — led by refineries and select banks on easing oil prices and improving US-Iran diplomatic signals. The backdrop is more mixed: August CPI accelerated to 11.15% y/y, the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5%, and the IMF has begun talks on the fourth EFF review, with up to $1.2bn potentially unlocked pending energy-sector and Sovereign Wealth Fund reforms.

GCC
Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI held at 56.6 (25th straight month of growth) and the UAE's hit 55.3, its fastest pace since December 2024 — both outrunning a Hormuz-driven disruption that has over 10 mb/d of Gulf oil output still shut in. PIF's board has approved its 2026-2030 strategy, shifting focus toward private-capital mobilisation as Vision 2030 matures.

GLOBAL
The Fed's hawkish tilt (25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% in September, more flagged by Governor Barr) is repricing the yield curve just as Washington widens its tariff agenda — a 100% duty on patented pharmaceuticals and expanded Section 338 tariffs on Canadian goods both take effect 29 September.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
🇵🇰 Sovereign Wealth Fund (Amendment) Bill before the Senate — governance wins, SOE oversight losses.
🌍 PIF's 2026-2030 strategy — non-oil diversification wins, Hormuz-exposed producers lose.
🌐 US pharma/Canada tariffs — domestic manufacturers win, import-reliant drugmakers and Canadian exporters lose.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 171,850 / pivot 172,232 / resistance 172,760, then 173,500. The desk stays constructively biased locally while watching Hormuz headlines and the US yield curve as the dominant global risk. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
